title: C. difficile: contact precautions (gown + nonsterile gloves)
vignette: An 86-year-old woman is hospitalized for a urinary tract infection due to Escherichia coli and is being treated with ceftriaxone. She has a history of advanced dementia, coronary artery disease, and congestive heart failure. On the fifth day of hospitalization, she seems agitated. The nurse reports that the patient had 3 episodes of watery diarrhea the previous night. Temperature is 38.3 C (100.9 F). In addition to appropriate hand hygiene, which of the following pieces of equipment are necessary before examining this patient?

clues.note: Recent broad-spectrum antibiotics disrupt colonic flora and are the key risk factor for Clostridioides difficile infection.
New-onset watery diarrhea a few days into antibiotics (with fever) strongly suggests C. difficile colitis.
Fever accompanying antibiotic-associated diarrhea supports C. difficile infection, which mandates CONTACT precautions.

whatMatters: New watery diarrhea + fever a few days into antibiotics = Clostridioides difficile infection. C. difficile requires CONTACT precautions: a GOWN plus NONSTERILE GLOVES for patient contact, and hand hygiene with SOAP AND WATER (alcohol sanitizers don't kill the spores). Answer A.
strategy: Recognize C. difficile (antibiotics -> watery diarrhea + fever), then recall its infection-control bundle: contact precautions = gown + nonsterile gloves; wash hands with soap and water (spores resist alcohol); private room preferred. Reject gloves-only (insufficient), sterile gloves/gown (needed for sterile procedures, not exams), and respirator (airborne precautions - TB/varicella, not C. difficile).

eliminations.label: Nonsterile gloves only - gown also required (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: gloves without a gown. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: contact precautions for C. difficile require BOTH nonsterile gloves AND a gown for any patient contact; gloves alone are insufficient. ✅ Correct if: standard precautions with no significant contamination risk.

eliminations.label: Respirator + sterile gloves + gown - airborne, not contact
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an N95 respirator (airborne precautions) plus sterile attire. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: C. difficile spreads by CONTACT (fecal-oral), not airborne; a respirator is for TB/measles/varicella. ✅ Correct if: airborne pathogens (tuberculosis, measles, varicella).

eliminations.label: Sterile gloves and gown - for procedures, not exams
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: sterile attire used to avoid contaminating a sterile field. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: sterile gear protects the PATIENT during procedures/surgery; contact precautions to protect the examiner use NONSTERILE gloves/gown. ✅ Correct if: a sterile procedure (e.g., central line placement).

eliminations.label: Sterile gloves only - wrong on both counts
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: sterile gloves without a gown. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: neither sterile gloves nor gloves-alone meets contact precautions (need nonsterile gloves + gown). ✅ Correct if: a minor sterile procedure, not this exam.

reasoning: Antibiotic exposure + new watery diarrhea + fever = Clostridioides difficile infection
Contact precautions = gown + nonsterile gloves; hand hygiene with soap and water (spores resist alcohol)
-> nonsterile gloves and gown; answer A
mechanism: Clostridioides difficile is a spore-forming, toxin-producing organism that overgrows the colon after antibiotics disrupt the normal flora, causing watery diarrhea, fever, and (in severe cases) pseudomembranous colitis. Because it spreads by the fecal-oral route via environmentally hardy SPORES, suspected or proven C. difficile requires CONTACT precautions on top of standard precautions: don a GOWN and NONSTERILE GLOVES for any patient contact, use dedicated equipment, and - critically - perform hand hygiene with SOAP AND WATER, because alcohol-based hand sanitizers do NOT kill C. difficile spores. A private room is preferred. Sterile gloves/gowns are meant to protect a sterile field during procedures (protecting the patient), not to protect the examiner from a contact pathogen, and airborne precautions with an N95 respirator are reserved for aerosol-transmitted organisms (tuberculosis, measles, varicella) - not C. difficile.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > C. difficile: antibiotic-associated diarrhea/pseudomembranous colitis, spores; CONTACT precautions (gown + nonsterile gloves), soap-and-water hand hygiene (alcohol ineffective on spores).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Antibiotic + watery diarrhea + fever = C. difficile -> contact precautions (gown + nonsterile gloves).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on contact vs airborne precautions, C. difficile spores, or sterile vs nonsterile gloves? Tell me which.

difficulty.text: Gloves-only is insufficient; sterile gear is for procedures; respirator is airborne (TB/measles/varicella), not C. difficile.

difficulty.text: Bank: C. difficile -> contact precautions (gown + nonsterile gloves) + soap-and-water handwash (spores resist alcohol).
